es: Presentar los puntos clave de una charla y responder a preguntas difíciles con matiz: pedir aclaración, admitir que no tienes un dato exacto, reconocer una objeción sin perder la conclusión y añadir una salvedad honesta.

prompt.es: Elige la mejor respuesta a la pregunta del oyente.

choices.text: By popular, I mean that over thirty students come every week.
Popular can mean many things, so I would rather not define it in numbers.
I'm afraid I don't have the exact figure, but the club is very popular.

feedback.es: Ante una pregunta sobre un término, lo mejor es definirlo con un dato concreto; las otras respuestas se declaran incapaces de definirlo o cambian de tema.

hint.es: Responde definiendo la palabra por la que te preguntan.

origin.text: An audience member asks: “What do you mean by popular?” You said that the club is popular, but you never defined the word.

prompt.es: Completa: «¿Podría aclarar su pregunta, por favor?»

feedback.es: Clarify (o rephrase) es el verbo para pedir que expliquen mejor una pregunta; va después de Could you.

origin.text: The question was long and confusing, so the speaker politely asked: “Could you ___ your question, please?”

prompt.es: Ordena: «Me temo que no tengo la cifra exacta, pero puedo comprobarla.»

answer.text: I'm afraid I don't have the exact figure but I can check

feedback.es: I'm afraid suaviza lo que no puedes dar y but I can check ofrece una salida honesta.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo responde la estudiante a la pregunta sobre los adultos.

choices.text: She accepts the point and says adults would surely show the same.
She accepts the point and admits her sample of teenagers limits her claim.
She dismisses the point, since her study was only about exam marks.

feedback.es: Acepta la pregunta como razonable, concede parte de la razón y reconoce el límite de su muestra (solo adolescentes) sin inventar una respuesta ni generalizar.

origin.audio: After the talk on sleep and exam marks, a teacher asked whether the results would be the same for adults. The student said that was a fair challenge and that, to a certain extent, the answer was yes, but she pointed out that her sample was made up of teenagers only, so she could not be sure. Then someone asked how many girls took part. She said she did not have an accurate number, but she promised to check the report and send the figure by email the next day.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del turno de preguntas con su función.

pairs: Off the top of my head, it was about fifty.
I can get back to you on that by email.

feedback.es: Cada fórmula resuelve una situación distinta: no entender, no recordar un dato, recibir una objeción o aplazar una respuesta.

pairs: Off the top of my head, it was about fifty.
I can get back to you on that by email.

prompt.es: Elige la respuesta más honesta y matizada a esta objeción.

choices.text: That is a fair challenge, and I admit my findings probably prove nothing at all.
You may be right, but I am certain the results are valid, so let us simply move on.
That is a fair challenge; I can't rule it out, but the trend held for both groups.

feedback.es: Reconoce la objeción, admite que no puede descartarla y aporta un dato (ambos grupos) que sostiene la conclusión; las otras respuestas lo conceden todo o se cierran con falsa seguridad.

origin.text: Question: “Could your findings simply show that the students who volunteered were already very good students?”

prompt.es: Elige la respuesta más adecuada a la pregunta del público.

choices.text: I'm afraid I can't say for certain: one small pilot elsewhere showed a similar pattern.
As far as I know, it is the same everywhere, although I haven't checked.
I'm afraid I can't say; we only studied one city, so there is nothing to add.

feedback.es: Admite el límite del estudio pero aprovecha el dato disponible; generalizar sin comprobar o descartar el piloto serían respuestas menos honestas.

origin.text: Question: “Is the trend the same in other cities?” Your study covered only one city, although a colleague's small pilot in a second city showed a similar pattern.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué da a entender la oradora con su respuesta.

choices.text: She is embarrassed that her research is incomplete.
She is honest about the limits of what she knows.
She doubts the trend because last winter's data is missing.

feedback.es: Prefiere no adivinar y comprobar el informe: muestra honestidad sobre lo que sabe, sin vergüenza ni dudas sobre la tendencia, que sigue sosteniendo.

origin.audio: Thank you for the question. To a certain extent, yes: the figures rose in both years. However, I'm afraid I don't have an accurate number for last winter, so I would rather not guess, and I will check the report this evening.

prompt.es: Completa: «Cuando empezaron a rebatir su conclusión, ella respondió con calma.»

feedback.es: Push back significa oponerse o rebatir; encaja con «objection» y con la actitud serena de la oradora.

origin.text: When several listeners began to ___ back against her conclusion, she thanked them and answered each objection calmly.

prompt.es: Escribe tu presentación final con dos respuestas matizadas.

answer.text: To sum up my talk, I presented a study of 120 students who slept eight hours a night for a month. Their marks rose steadily, from 7.1 to 7.8, and the effect was clear for most of them. Now let me answer your two questions. First, you asked how many of the students were girls. Off the top of my head, it was around half, but I'm afraid I don't have the exact figure, so I would need to check the report before I give you an accurate number. Second, you asked whether these students were simply better students already. That is a fair challenge. To a certain extent you may be right, because the students chose to take part. However, the marks of the same students rose during the study, so the findings suggest that sleep may help, although I would add one caveat: the sample was small, and more research is needed before we can be sure. I can give you more detail after the talk, and I will send the full figures by email. Thank you for your questions.
accepted: To sum up my talk, I presented a study of 120 students who slept eight hours a night for a month. Their marks rose steadily, from 7.1 to 7.8, and the effect was clear for most of them. Now let me answer your two questions. First, you asked how many of the students were girls. Off the top of my head, it was around half, but I'm afraid I don't have the exact figure, so I would need to check the report before I give you an accurate number. Second, you asked whether these students were simply better students already. That is a fair challenge. To a certain extent you may be right, because the students chose to take part. However, the marks of the same students rose during the study, so the findings suggest that sleep may help, although I would add one caveat: the sample was small, and more research is needed before we can be sure. I can give you more detail after the talk, and I will send the full figures by email. Thank you for your questions.

Let me summarise the main points of my talk. We studied 120 students for a month. Those who slept eight hours scored higher, and their mark went up from 7.1 to 7.8. Thank you for your two questions. About the first one, how many girls took part, I'm afraid I can't give an accurate number now, but I can check it and send you the figure later. About the second one, it could be argued that these students were already better, and that is a fair point. However, the same students improved during the month, so the results seem to show a real effect. It is likely to be valid for students of our age, although I would not say it is certain, and I would add one caveat: the sample was small. I can give you more detail after the talk, and I will send the full numbers by email this week.

feedback.es: Una buena respuesta resume la charla con tendencia y cifras, admite con honestidad que no tienes un dato exacto, y reconoce la objeción sin perder la conclusión.

origin.text: Caso: acabas de presentar un estudio sobre 120 estudiantes que durmieron ocho horas durante un mes; su nota media subió de 7,1 a 7,8. El público te hace dos preguntas: 1) «¿Cuántas chicas participaron?» (no recuerdas la cifra exacta) y 2) «¿No serían ya mejores estudiantes?». Escribe entre 210 y 260 palabras: un resumen con la tendencia y las cifras, y dos respuestas con matiz (una salvedad incluida).

evidenceGroups: off the top of my head

prompt.es: ¿Qué actitud muestra el orador ante la objeción sobre la muestra?

choices.text: He accepts the limitation and drops his claim entirely.
He regrets the small sample but says it proves the pattern anyway.
He accepts the limitation and keeps his claim cautious.

feedback.es: Reconoce que la muestra era pequeña y por eso presentó el patrón como provisional («tentative»): acepta la limitación y mantiene una afirmación prudente, sin retirarla ni exagerarla.

origin.text: An audience member says: “Your figures look good, but aren't they just the result of a small sample?” The speaker answers: “You're right to ask. The sample size was small, which is why I described the pattern as tentative rather than certain.”

prompt.es: Ordena: «Puedo enviarle la cifra exacta por correo mañana por la mañana.»

answer.text: I can send you the exact figure by email tomorrow morning

feedback.es: I can send you + complemento ofrece una respuesta posterior; by email y tomorrow morning fijan cómo y cuándo.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hace el orador ante la pregunta.

choices.text: He admits what his data cannot show and adds cautious context.
He admits his data are limited and says the question is unimportant.
He treats earlier studies as proof, so his own data hardly matter.

feedback.es: Dice que sus datos no responden la pregunta y aporta solo un contexto prudente («as far as I know»): ni resta importancia a la pregunta ni presenta esos estudios como prueba.

origin.audio: Honestly, my data cannot answer that question. What I can say is that, as far as I know, earlier studies point in the same direction, although I would not go any further than that.
